facts.statement: The genus Georgiasaurus was described by Otschev in 1977.
The name Georgiasaurus means "Georgy's lizard" and honors the author's father, Georgy Otschev, who died before the 1976 publication.
facts.quote: Georgiasaurus ("Georgy's lizard"; after V. A. Otschev's father, Georgy Otschev, a geodesist who died shortly before Otschev published the description in 1976)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen POKM 11658 originally contained a complete skeleton but was damaged during quarry stone preparation.
facts.quote: Originally a complete skeleton, the specimen, holotype POKM 11658 consisting of seven neck vertebrae, vertebral impressions, both scapulae and two limbs, was damaged in preparation of the quarry stone.

facts.statement: The fossil remains were discovered near the village of Zatolokino.
facts.quote: It was found near the village of Zatolokino.

facts.statement: Georgiasaurus was a large polycotylid plesiosaur that measured between 4 and 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a fairly large polycotylid, measuring 4 - 5 m long.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Georgiasaurus at 450 kg.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated its weight at 450 kg.

facts.statement: Georgiasaurus belongs to the subfamily Polycotylinae.
The genus Georgiasaurus is classified within the family Polycotylidae.
Georgiasaurus lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)
